questions.question: Which of the following awards was won by Lata Mangeshkar in the year 2001?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharat Ratna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lata Mangeshkar** is one of the most renowned playback singers in India, known for her melodious voice and a vast repertoire of songs in various Indian languages.
 
• She was awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, in the year **2001** for her exceptional contribution to Indian music and arts.
 
• The Bharat Ratna is awarded in recognition of exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavour.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar is often referred to as the** Swar Kokila** for her contribution to Indian music over several decades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award**

 
 
• This award is presented by Filmfare as part of its annual Filmfare Awards for Hindi films.
 
• It is given to individuals for their outstanding contribution to the Indian film industry over their lifetime.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar received this award in 1993.
 
 
 
• **Padma Vibhushan**
 
 
• It is the second-highest civilian award in India, given for exceptional and distinguished service.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar was honored with the Padma Vibhushan in 1999.
 
 
 
• **Dadasaheb Phalke Award**
 
 
• This is India's highest award in cinema, presented annually at the National Film Awards ceremony by the Directorate of Film Festivals.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1989 for her outstanding contribution to the growth and development of Indian cinema.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Ratna**
 
 
• The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of India, instituted in 1954.
 
• It is conferred for exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavour.
 
• The award does not carry any monetary grant or pension but is a recognition of the highest degree of service to the nation.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

questions.question: Which article has a similar provision to that of Article 32 and deals with writ jurisdiction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 226**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 226** of the Indian Constitution empowers the High Courts to issue certain writs.
 
• This Article extends the writ jurisdiction to all cases where a fundamental right is violated, as well as other legal rights.
 
• Article 226 can be invoked not only for the enforcement of fundamental rights but also for any other purpose.
 
• The power conferred by Article 226 is wider in scope as compared to Article 32, which is restricted to the enforcement of Fundamental Rights only.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 32**

 
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to constitutional remedies, allowing individuals to move the Supreme Court directly in case of violation of fundamental rights.
 
• It is known as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution as described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• The Supreme Court can issue writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• This Article is a crucial provision for the protection of Fundamental Rights in India.
 
 
 
• **Writs**
 
 
• A writ is a formal written order issued by a court.
 
• Types of writs include habeas corpus (to produce the body), mandamus (to command), prohibition (to forbid), quo warranto (by what authority), and certiorari (to be informed).
 
• These writs are powerful tools in the hands of the judiciary to ensure the protection of rights and to enforce public duties.
 
 
 
• **High Courts**
 
 
• High Courts are the principal civil courts of original jurisdiction in each state and union territory.
 
• They also have appellate jurisdiction over the subordinate courts.
 
• High Courts have the power to issue writs under Article 226 for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for other purposes.
 
• Their jurisdiction is broader compared to the Supreme Court in terms of issuing writs.

questions.question: Who among the following formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was a prominent peasant leader in India and was deeply involved in the peasant movement.
 
• He founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS) in 1929 to address the issues of peasants and farmers in Bihar.
 
• The BPKS played a crucial role in mobilizing peasants against the zamindari system and for the rights of tenant farmers.
 
• Swami Sahajanand Saraswati later became the president of the All India Kisan Sabha, a nationwide peasant organization, further amplifying his influence in the peasant movement in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peasant Movement in India:**

 
 
• The peasant movement in India was a series of political movements for the rights of the agricultural workers and against the feudal land system.
 
• These movements were significant in shaping the agrarian policies of the country and addressing issues like land reforms, tenancy rights, and fair wages.
 
 
 
• **Zamindari System:**
 
 
• The Zamindari system was a traditional land revenue system in India where landlords or zamindars collected rent from the peasants and paid a portion to the British colonial government.
 
• This system led to the exploitation of peasants, high rents, and forced labor, causing widespread agrarian distress.
 
 
 
• **All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS):**
 
 
• The AIKS was formed in 1936 as a national organization to address the issues faced by peasants across India.
 
• It worked towards the abolition of the zamindari system, fair land distribution, and better living conditions for agricultural workers.
 
 
 
• **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati's Contributions:**
 
 
• He was a key figure in the peasant movement and worked tirelessly for the upliftment of the agrarian community.
 
• His efforts led to significant reforms in the agrarian sector, and he is remembered as a champion of peasant rights in India.

questions.question: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmaram Pandurang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atmaram Pandurang was a social reformer and the founder of the **Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867.**
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was a movement for religious and social reform in Maharashtra based on earlier reform movements.
 
• The organization aimed to make people believe in one God and discard the caste system and superstitions.
 
• Atmaram Pandurang's efforts were directed towards promoting women's education and widow remarriage and opposing child marriage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prarthana Samaj**

 
 
• Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj founded by** Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Bengal.**
 
• It was established by Atmaram Pandurang in 1867 to reform the social practices and religious beliefs of the Hindus in Maharashtra.
 
• The Samaj's principles were based on the teachings of Christianity and the ancient Hindu scriptures, advocating monotheism and discarding idol worship.
 
• Prominent members of the Prarthana Samaj included Justice** Mahadev Govind Ranade, R.G. Bhandarkar, and N.G. Chandavarkar**, who played significant roles in the social reform movements in Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj**
 
 
• Founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 in Kolkata,** Brahmo Samaj was one of the earliest reform movements in India.
 
• The Samaj aimed at purifying Hinduism and promoting monotheism, rejecting the caste system, idol worship, and rituals.
 
• It played a crucial role in the abolition of the practice of Sati and child marriage, and the promotion of widow remarriage and women's education.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is often called the **"Father of Modern India**" due to his efforts to modernize Indian society.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Movements in India**
 
 
• During the** 19th and early 20th centuries,** India witnessed several social reform movements aimed at addressing social issues like caste discrimination, gender inequality, and religious superstitions.
 
• Prominent social reformers included** Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Jyotirao Phule, and Swami Vivekananda.**
 
• These movements played a significant role in shaping modern Indian society by advocating for education, women's rights, and social equality.
 
• The reforms laid the groundwork for India's struggle for independence and the subsequent formation of a democratic and secular nation.

questions.question: Who among the following has authored the play 'Nil Darpan'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dinabandhu Mitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dinabandhu Mitra was a notable Bengali dramatist of the 19th century.
 
• He wrote the play 'Nil Darpan' in 1860-61, which portrays the plight of indigo farmers under British rule in Bengal.
 
• 'Nil Darpan' is considered a significant work in Bengali literature and played a crucial role in the Indigo revolt of 1859-60.
 
• The play was translated into English by Reverend James Long, which led to his imprisonment and fine due to its anti-British sentiments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indigo Rebellion:**

 
 
• The Indigo Rebellion (or Indigo Revolt) was a peasant movement and subsequent uprising against indigo planters in Bengal in 1859-60.
 
• Indigo farmers were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions and received meager payment.
 
• The rebellion highlighted the exploitation by British planters and led to reforms in the indigo cultivation practices.
 
 
 
• **Bengali Literature:**
 
 
• Bengali literature is one of the richest literary traditions in the Indian subcontinent, with works dating back to the 10th century.
 
• It encompasses a wide range of genres, including poetry, drama, novels, short stories, and essays.
 
• Notable figures in Bengali literature include Rabindranath Tagore, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, and Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay.
 
 
 
• **British Colonial Rule in India:**
 
 
• British colonial rule in India lasted from 1858 to 1947, following the transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown after the Revolt of 1857.
 
• During this period, India was subjected to economic exploitation, cultural changes, and political reorganization.
 
• Significant events during British rule include the establishment of the Indian National Congress, the Partition of Bengal, and the struggle for Indian independence led by figures like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Subhas Chandra Bose.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct order of basicity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CsOH > KOH > NaOH > LiOH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The basicity of alkali metal hydroxides increases as we move down the group in the periodic table.
 
• This is because the ionic nature and size of the cation increase as we move down the group.
 
• CsOH is the most basic among the given hydroxides because cesium is at the bottom of the alkali metal group.
 
• LiOH is the least basic because lithium is at the top of the alkali metal group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basicity:**

 
 
• Basicity refers to the ability of a substance to accept protons (H+ ions) or donate a pair of valence electrons to form a bond.
 
• In the context of alkali metal hydroxides, basicity is determined by the extent to which the hydroxide ion (OH-) is available to react with acids.
 
 
 
• **Alkali Metal Hydroxides:**
 
 
• Alkali metal hydroxides are compounds formed by alkali metals (Group 1 elements) and hydroxide ions (OH-).
 
• Examples include LiOH (Lithium Hydroxide), NaOH (Sodium Hydroxide), KOH (Potassium Hydroxide), and CsOH (Cesium Hydroxide).
 
• These hydroxides are strong bases and are highly soluble in water.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Trends:**
 
 
• As we move down Group 1 in the periodic table, the size of the alkali metal cations increases.
 
• This leads to a decrease in the lattice energy of the hydroxides, making them more soluble and hence more basic.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Nature:**
 
 
• The ionic nature of a compound refers to the extent to which it dissociates into ions in a solution.
 
• Alkali metal hydroxides dissociate completely in water, releasing hydroxide ions, which contribute to their basicity.

questions.question: In which city was the first golf club of India situated?

questions.question: What challenge does foreign investment often face in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inconsistent regulatory environment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The regulatory environment in India is often perceived as **inconsistent** and subject to frequent changes, making it difficult for foreign investors to plan long-term investments.
 
• Issues such as **complex tax laws**, **bureaucratic red tape**, and sudden changes in policies can create uncertainty for foreign businesses.
 
• The **lack of a unified regulatory framework** across different states in India further complicates the investment landscape for foreign companies.
 
• Foreign investors may face challenges related to **compliance** with diverse and sometimes conflicting regulations at the central and state levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**

 
 
• FDI refers to investments made by a company or individual in one country into business interests located in another country.
 
• This type of investment generally involves a significant degree of control and influence over the foreign business.
 
• FDI can provide a number of benefits to the host country, including capital inflow, technology transfer, and job creation.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Environment**
 
 
• The regulatory environment encompasses the laws, regulations, and policies that govern business operations in a country.
 
• A stable and predictable regulatory environment is crucial for attracting and retaining foreign investment.
 
• Key regulatory aspects include taxation, labor laws, environmental regulations, and business registration processes.
 
 
 
• **Bureaucratic Red Tape**
 
 
• Bureaucratic red tape refers to the excessive and often unnecessary regulations and procedures that can hinder business operations.
 
• It can include lengthy approval processes, complex documentation requirements, and inefficient administrative procedures.
 
• Reducing bureaucratic red tape is important for creating a more business-friendly environment and encouraging investment.
 
 
 
• **Policy Stability**
 
 
• Policy stability refers to the consistency and predictability of government policies over time.
 
• Frequent changes in policies can create uncertainty and risk for investors, making it difficult to plan and execute long-term investments.
 
• Ensuring policy stability is important for building investor confidence and attracting foreign investment.

questions.question: Mohan Veena player, Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won the __________ Award in the year 1994.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grammy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt is an Indian classical musician who plays the Mohan Veena, a modified slide guitar.
 
• He won the Grammy Award in 1994 for his album "A Meeting by the River" in collaboration with Ry Cooder.
 
• The Grammy Awards are presented by the Recording Academy to recognize achievements in the music industry.
 
• Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt's Grammy win brought global recognition to Indian classical music and the Mohan Veena.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grammy Awards**

 
 
• The Grammy Awards, or simply Grammys, are awards presented by the Recording Academy to recognize outstanding achievements in the music industry.
 
• The awards were first presented in 1959, and they are considered one of the most prestigious awards in the music industry.
 
• Categories include Best New Artist, Album of the Year, Record of the Year, and Song of the Year, among others.
 
• The Grammy Awards ceremony is held annually, and it features performances by prominent artists, as well as the presentation of those awards that have a more popular interest.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt**
 
 
• Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt is a renowned Indian classical musician known for his expertise in playing the Mohan Veena.
 
• The Mohan Veena is a modified version of the Hawaiian guitar, incorporating elements of the sitar and the veena to suit Indian classical music.
 
• Pandit Bhatt has received numerous awards and honors for his contribution to music, including the Padma Shri and the Padma Bhushan from the Government of India.
 
• His collaboration with American guitarist Ry Cooder on the album "A Meeting by the River" earned him the Grammy Award for Best World Music Album in 1994.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists in the field of performing arts, including music, dance, and drama.
 
• It is awarded annually by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.
 
• The award consists of a purse, a tamrapatra (a brass plaque), and a shawl.
 
• Many renowned artists in India, including musicians, dancers, and theater artists, have been recipients of this prestigious award.

questions.question: Lathmar Holi is primarily celebrated in the state of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lathmar Holi** is a unique and traditional form of Holi celebration primarily observed in the towns of **Barsana and Nandgaon** in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• This festival is celebrated a few days before the main Holi festival and involves women playfully beating men with sticks, hence the name 'Lathmar' which translates to 'beating with sticks'.
 
• The celebration is rooted in the legend of **Radha and Krishna**, where Krishna visited Radha's village and teased her and her friends, leading to the women chasing him away with sticks.
 
• The festival attracts numerous tourists and devotees who come to witness and participate in the vibrant and joyful celebrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Holi Festival**

 
 
• Holi, also known as the 'Festival of Colors', is an ancient Hindu festival celebrated predominantly in India and Nepal.
 
• The festival signifies the victory of good over evil, the arrival of spring, and the end of winter. It also serves as a thanksgiving for a good harvest.
 
• The celebrations begin with a Holika bonfire on the night before Holi, where people gather, sing, dance, and perform rituals.
 
• The following day is celebrated with vibrant colors, water balloons, and traditional sweets. It is a day of festivity and joy, bringing people together to forgive and forget past grievances.
 
 
 
• **Radha and Krishna**
 
 
• Radha and Krishna are central figures in Hindu mythology and are considered the epitome of divine love.
 
• Krishna, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu, is known for his playful and mischievous nature, while Radha symbolizes the ultimate devotee and beloved of Krishna.
 
• Their love story is celebrated in various cultural and religious contexts, including dance, music, and festivals like Holi.
 
• The stories of their divine love have inspired countless artistic and literary works in Indian culture.
 
 
 
• **Braj Region**
 
 
• Braj, also known as Brij or Braj Bhoomi, is a region in Uttar Pradesh associated with the childhood and youthful pastimes of Lord Krishna.
 
• It includes important pilgrimage sites like Mathura, Vrindavan, Govardhan, Gokul, and Barsana.
 
• The region is known for its rich cultural heritage, including traditional music, dance, and festivals dedicated to Krishna.
 
• Braj attracts millions of devotees and tourists annually, making it a significant religious and cultural destination in India.

questions.question: When the analysis of population density is done by calculating it through net cultivated area, then the measure is termed as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Physiological density**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Physiological density is a measure of population density that refers to the number of people per unit area of arable land.
 
• This measure provides insights into the pressure exerted by the population on the productive land area.
 
• It helps in understanding the carrying capacity of the land and the potential challenges in terms of food production and resource management.
 
• Physiological density is considered more meaningful than simple population density (people per total land area) because it focuses on the land that can actually support human life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Density**

 
 
• Agricultural density is a measure of the number of farmers per unit area of arable land.
 
• This metric helps in understanding the agricultural efficiency and the potential output of the farming sector.
 
• It provides insights into the level of development and technological advancement in agriculture within a region.
 
• Higher agricultural density may indicate less mechanization and more labor-intensive agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Gross Density**
 
 
• Gross density refers to the total population divided by the total land area.
 
• This measure does not differentiate between arable and non-arable land, giving an overall view of population distribution.
 
• It is useful for general demographic studies and urban planning purposes.
 
• However, it may not accurately reflect the actual human impact on the productive land resources.
 
 
 
• **Net Density**
 
 
• Net density is a less commonly used term and is not a standard measure in population geography.
 
• It might refer to a refined measure of population density considering specific criteria or exclusions.
 
• In most contexts, "net density" is not clearly defined or widely recognized.
 
• It is important to refer to more standardized measures like physiological or agricultural density for accurate analysis.

questions.question: Which Indian among the following has his name in Time Magazine's list of '100 most influential people of 2021'?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• As the Prime Minister of India since 2014, Modi has implemented several major reforms and initiatives aimed at enhancing India's economic and social landscapes.
 
• His notable initiatives include the Digital India campaign, Make in India, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, and Atmanirbhar Bharat, which have been influential in shaping India's development trajectory.
 
• Modi's leadership during the COVID-19 pandemic, including the rollout of the vaccination program and economic relief measures, has also been a key factor in his inclusion in the list.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Time Magazine's 100 Most Influential People**

 
 
• Time Magazine's list of the 100 most influential people is an annual ranking that recognizes the contributions and impact of various individuals across different fields.
 
• The list includes leaders, innovators, artists, and icons who have made significant strides in their respective domains and have had a profound influence on the world stage.
 
• Being featured in this list is considered a prestigious honor, highlighting the individual's influence and achievements on a global scale.
 
• The list is divided into various categories, including leaders, pioneers, titans, artists, and icons, reflecting the diverse areas of influence and impact.
 
 
 
• **Narendra Modi's Major Initiatives**
 
 
• **Digital India:** A campaign launched to ensure the government's services are made available to citizens electronically by improving online infrastructure and increasing Internet connectivity.
 
• **Make in India:** An initiative aimed at transforming India into a global manufacturing hub by encouraging both multinational and domestic companies to manufacture their products in India.

questions.question: Who is Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology as of July 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jitendra Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jitendra Singh is the Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology as of July 2023.
 
• He has been serving in this position since his appointment by the Prime Minister.
 
• Jitendra Singh is also known for his roles in various other ministries, including the Ministry of Earth Sciences and the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances, and Pensions.
 
• He has been actively involved in promoting scientific research and development in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Minister of State (Independent Charge)**

 
 
• In the Indian government, a Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) is a minister who is in charge of a ministry without an overseeing cabinet minister.
 
• These ministers have the same responsibilities as cabinet ministers in their respective ministries but report directly to the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Science and Technology**
 
 
• This ministry is responsible for the promotion of science and technology in India.
 
• It encompasses several departments, including the Department of Science and Technology (DST), the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), and the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR).
 
• The ministry aims to boost scientific research, innovation, and development in various fields such as space, biotechnology, and renewable energy.
 
 
 
• **Jitendra Singh**
 
 
• Jitendra Singh is an Indian politician and a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• He has held various significant positions in the government, contributing to policies and initiatives in multiple sectors.
 
• He is known for his work in improving governance and administration, as well as fostering scientific advancements in the country.

questions.question: Which plateaus are very fertile because they are rich in black soil that is very good for farming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan lava plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Deccan lava plateau is known for its **black soil**, also called regur soil, which is ideal for growing cotton and other crops.
 
• This region is one of the most fertile areas in India, making it a crucial agricultural zone.
 
• The black soil in the Deccan lava plateau retains moisture, which is beneficial for farming even during dry seasons.
 
• The soil is rich in essential nutrients like calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime, which support diverse agricultural activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Black Soil**

 
 
• Also known as regur soil, black soil is formed from volcanic rocks and lava-flow areas.
 
• This type of soil is highly moisture-retentive and is rich in iron, lime, calcium, potassium, aluminum, and magnesium.
 
• Black soil is predominantly found in the Deccan plateau, including parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is especially suited for growing cotton, and thus it is also called "cotton soil."
 
 
 
• **Deccan Plateau**
 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau in western and southern India, covering about 500,000 square kilometers.
 
• It is bounded by the Western Ghats on the west, the Eastern Ghats on the east, and the Satpura and Vindhya ranges to the north.
 
• The plateau is composed of ancient crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks.
 
• The region experiences a semi-arid climate with distinct dry and wet seasons.
 
 
 
• **Fertility of Soil**
 
 
• Soil fertility refers to the ability of soil to sustain agricultural plant growth, i.e., to provide plant habitat and result in sustained and consistent yields of high quality.
 
• Fertile soil contains essential nutrients for plant growth, including nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
 
• Other factors influencing soil fertility include soil structure, organic matter content, pH level, and moisture retention capacity.
 
• In agricultural practices, soil fertility is enhanced by adding organic and inorganic fertilizers, crop rotation, and other soil management practices.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a condition for the President's office in India?

options.text: He shall not be entitled, without payment of rent, to use his official residence.
He shall not be a member of either House of the Parliament.
The allowances shall not be diminished during his term of office.
He shall not hold any office of profit.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He shall not be entitled, without payment of rent, to use his official residence.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India is entitled to use his official residence, Rashtrapati Bhavan, without any payment of rent.
 
• According to Article 59 of the Indian Constitution, the President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or a House of the Legislature of any State.
 
• During the term of office, the President's emoluments and allowances cannot be diminished as per Article 59(3).
 
• The President shall not hold any office of profit during his term as mentioned in Article 59(4).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 59 of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• It outlines the conditions of the President's office in India.
 
• The President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or a House of the Legislature of any State.
 
• The President shall not hold any other office of profit.
 
• The President's emoluments and allowances cannot be diminished during his term of office.
 
 
 
• **Rashtrapati Bhavan**
 
 
• It is the official residence of the President of India.
 
• Located in New Delhi, it was formerly known as the Viceroy's House.
 
• Rashtrapati Bhavan includes the main building, large gardens, staff quarters, stables, and other offices.
 
 
 
• **Office of Profit**
 
 
• An office of profit is a position that brings financial gain, advantage, or benefit.
 
• The President is not allowed to hold any office of profit to ensure independence and impartiality.

questions.question: Which of the following states is the biggest producer of Pulses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is the largest producer of pulses in India.
 
• The state contributes significantly to the total production of pulses in the country.
 
• The major pulses grown in Madhya Pradesh include chickpeas (gram), pigeon peas (arhar/tur), lentils, and moong beans.
 
• Madhya Pradesh has favorable climatic conditions and soil types that support the cultivation of a variety of pulses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulses**

 
 
• Pulses are an important group of crops that belong to the legume family.
 
• They are a rich source of protein, dietary fiber, vitamins, and minerals, making them an essential part of a balanced diet.
 
• Pulses are also known for their ability to fix nitrogen in the soil, which improves soil fertility and reduces the need for chemical fertilizers.
 
• Common types of pulses include chickpeas, lentils, beans, peas, and pigeon peas.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture in Madhya Pradesh**
 
 
• Madhya Pradesh is known as the "Heart of India" due to its geographical location.
 
• The state has a diverse agro-climatic condition that supports the cultivation of a wide range of crops.
 
• Apart from pulses, Madhya Pradesh is also a leading producer of wheat, soybean, and oilseeds in India.
 
• The state government has implemented various agricultural schemes and policies to support farmers and enhance agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Pulses in India**
 
 
• India is the largest producer and consumer of pulses in the world.
 
• Pulses play a crucial role in ensuring food security and nutrition in the country.
 
• They are a key component of the Indian diet, especially for vegetarians who rely on pulses as a primary source of protein.
 
• The cultivation of pulses also contributes to sustainable agricultural practices and environmental conservation.

questions.question: __________ is an industry association and self-regulatory organisation (SRO) whose primary objective is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Microfinance Institutions Network**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) is an industry association that represents the microfinance industry in India.
 
• It is a self-regulatory organization (SRO) recognized by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• The primary objective of MFIN is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector by promoting responsible lending practices and ensuring client protection.
 
• MFIN also works on policy advocacy, capacity building, and facilitating knowledge sharing among its members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-help Group Association**

 
 
• Self-help groups (SHGs) are small voluntary associations of people, typically women, who come together to form a group for the purpose of savings and credit.
 
• SHGs promote savings among members and use the pooled resources to provide small loans to members.
 
• They play a crucial role in financial inclusion and empowerment of marginalized communities, especially women.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance and Investments Regulatory Authority**
 
 
• There is no known regulatory authority by this name specifically for microfinance and investments in India.
 
• Microfinance institutions in India are primarily regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
 
 
• **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)**
 
 
• NABARD is an apex development bank in India, established to provide and regulate credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of agriculture, small-scale industries, cottage and village industries, handicrafts, and other rural crafts.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in the development of the rural sector in India.
 
• While NABARD supports microfinance activities, it is not an industry association or SRO specifically for the microfinance sector.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the grade of organisation and its example?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Tissue-organ grade organisation - Euplectella**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cellular grade organisation** refers to a level of organization where cells are functionally differentiated but do not form tissues. Sycon is an example of this grade.
 
• **Protoplasmic grade organisation** is the simplest level of organisation where all life functions are confined within a single cell. Paramecium is an example of this grade.
 
• **Cell-tissue grade organisation** involves groups of similar cells performing a common function. Jellyfish represent this grade.
 
• **Tissue-organ grade organisation** refers to tissues grouped into organs, each performing different functions.** **
 
 
• ​**Euplectella** (Venus's flower basket) is a type of glass **sponge** and does not exhibit tissue-organ grade organization. Instead, it is an example of cellular grade organization, characteristic of Porifera (sponges), where the organization is primarily at the cellular level and not organized into true tissues and organs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cellular Grade Organisation**

 
 
• This refers to organisms whose body is made up of cells that are functionally differentiated but do not form true tissues.
 
• Sponges (Porifera) like Sycon exhibit this type of organisation.
 
• These organisms have a simple body structure with cells specialized for different functions such as feeding, reproduction, and protection.
 
 
 
• **Protoplasmic Grade Organisation**
 
 
• It is the simplest level of organization where all life functions occur within a single cell.
 
• Protozoans like Paramecium demonstrate this type of organization.
 
• These organisms are unicellular and perform all necessary life processes within one cell.
 
 
 
• **Cell-Tissue Grade Organisation**
 
 
• Organisms with this level of organisation have cells grouped into tissues.
 
• Coelenterates, such as jellyfish, exhibit this type of organisation.
 
• These organisms have more complex structures with different tissues performing various functions.
 
 
 
• **Tissue-Organ Grade Organisation**
 
 
• This level of organisation involves tissues grouped into organs, each performing specific functions.
 
• Euplectella, a genus of glass sponges, is an example of cellular grade organisation grade.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best defines the monoecious?

options.text: A flower with both androecium and gynoecium

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A flower with both androecium and gynoecium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Monoecious plants** have both male (androecium) and female (gynoecium) reproductive organs in the same plant.
 
• This characteristic allows monoecious plants to self-pollinate, although cross-pollination can also occur.
 
• Examples of monoecious plants include maize, cucumbers, and squash.
 
• Monoecious plants are different from dioecious plants, which have male and female reproductive organs on separate plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Androecium**

 
 
• The androecium is the male reproductive part of a flower.
 
• It consists of stamens, each of which has a filament topped by an anther where pollen is produced.
 
 
 
• **Gynoecium**
 
 
• The gynoecium is the female reproductive part of a flower.
 
• It consists of one or more carpels, each containing an ovary, style, and stigma.
 
• The ovary contains ovules, which develop into seeds upon fertilization.
 
 
 
• **Dioecious**
 
 
• Dioecious plants have male and female reproductive organs on separate plants.
 
• This means that a dioecious plant is either male or female, not both.
 
• Examples of dioecious plants include holly, willow, and asparagus.
 
 
 
• **Pollination**
 
 
• Pollination is the process by which pollen is transferred from the male part of a plant to the female part, allowing fertilization to occur.
 
• Pollination can be carried out by wind, water, insects, birds, and other animals.
 
• Self-pollination occurs within the same flower or plant, while cross-pollination occurs between different plants.

questions.question: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1973**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Project Tiger** was launched by the Government of India on **1st April 1973**.
 
• The aim of this initiative was to ensure a viable population of Bengal tigers in their natural habitats and to protect them from extinction.
 
• This project is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).
 
• Initially, nine tiger reserves were covered under this project, which has now expanded to cover more than 50 tiger reserves across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**

 
 
• The NTCA was constituted under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, as amended in 2006, for strengthening tiger conservation.
 
• It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
 
• The NTCA is responsible for the implementation of Project Tiger to ensure the protection of tigers.
 
• It regularly assesses tiger populations, habitat status, and the success of conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**
 
 
• This Act was enacted by the Indian Parliament to ensure the protection of wild animals, birds, and plants.
 
• It aims to safeguard the country's ecological and environmental security.
 
• The Act provides for the creation of protected areas such as national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.
 
• It also lays down the legal framework for the protection and management of wildlife habitats.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Bengal Tigers**
 
 
• Bengal tigers (Panthera tigris tigris) are native to the Indian subcontinent and are classified as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
 
• Efforts to conserve Bengal tigers include anti-poaching measures, habitat restoration, and community involvement.
 
• India is home to more than 70% of the world's wild tiger population.
 
• Effective conservation strategies have led to an increase in the tiger population in recent years.

questions.question: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposition of calcium carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The decomposition of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) results in the formation of calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂).
 
• This reaction is represented by the equation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.
 
• The oxidation states of the elements do not change during this decomposition reaction, indicating it is not a redox reaction.
 
• In contrast, decomposition reactions that are redox reactions involve changes in the oxidation states of the participating elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition Reactions**

 
 
• A decomposition reaction is a type of chemical reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler compounds or elements.
 
• These reactions often require an input of energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity.
 
• Examples include the decomposition of water into hydrogen and oxygen (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂) and the decomposition of potassium chlorate into potassium chloride and oxygen (2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂).
 
 
 
• **Redox Reactions**
 
 
• Redox reactions, or oxidation-reduction reactions, involve the transfer of electrons between two substances.
 
• Oxidation refers to the loss of electrons, while reduction refers to the gain of electrons.
 
• In a redox reaction, one substance is oxidized (loses electrons) and another is reduced (gains electrons).
 
• An example is the decomposition of sodium hydride (NaH), where NaH decomposes into sodium metal (Na) and hydrogen gas (H₂), with sodium being reduced and hydrogen being oxidized.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation States**
 
 
• The oxidation state (or number) of an element in a compound is a measure of the degree of oxidation of that element.
 
• It is defined as the charge an atom would have if all bonds were completely ionic.
 
• Changes in oxidation states during a reaction indicate a redox process.

questions.question: The head office of Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is located in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is the national governing body for cricket in India.
 
• The BCCI headquarters is located at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
 
• Mumbai is known as the cricket capital of India, having produced many legendary cricketers.
 
• The BCCI was formed in December 1928 and is affiliated with the International Cricket Council (ICC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India)**

 
 
• The BCCI is the wealthiest cricket board in the world, managing the Indian cricket team and organizing domestic and international cricket matches in India.
 
• It oversees cricketing activities in India and has the authority to select players, umpires, and officials to participate in international cricket events.
 
• The BCCI also organizes the Indian Premier League (IPL), one of the world's most popular and lucrative T20 cricket leagues.
 
• It is responsible for developing cricket infrastructure and promoting the sport at all levels in the country.
 
 
 
• **Wankhede Stadium**
 
 
• Wankhede Stadium, located in Mumbai, is one of the most iconic cricket stadiums in India.
 
• The stadium has hosted numerous memorable cricket matches, including the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup final, where India emerged victorious.
 
• It has a seating capacity of around 33,000 spectators and serves as the home ground for the Mumbai cricket team and the Mumbai Indians (IPL team).
 
• Named after Sheshrao Krishnarao Wankhede, a politician and the then President of the Mumbai Cricket Association, the stadium was established in 1974.
 
 
 
• **International Cricket Council (ICC)**
 
 
• The ICC is the global governing body for cricket, responsible for overseeing and regulating the international game.
 
• Headquartered in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, the ICC organizes major international cricket tournaments like the ICC Cricket World Cup, ICC T20 World Cup, and ICC Champions Trophy.
 
• The ICC ensures that the rules and regulations of cricket are uniformly followed by its member countries.
 
• It also appoints match officials for international matches and works towards the development and promotion of cricket worldwide.

questions.question: Who is the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu as of July 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MK Stalin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• M.K. Stalin is the current Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, having assumed office on May 7, 2021.
 
• He is the son of the former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, M. Karunanidhi.
 
• Stalin is a prominent leader of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party.
 
• Under his leadership, the DMK won the 2021 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly election, securing a majority of the seats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)**

 
 
• DMK is a major political party in the state of Tamil Nadu and the union territory of Puducherry.
 
• It was founded by C.N. Annadurai in 1949 as a breakaway faction from the Dravidar Kazhagam (DK) led by Periyar E.V. Ramasamy.
 
• The party's ideologies are centered on social justice, self-respect, and Tamil nationalism.
 
• DMK has been a dominant force in Tamil Nadu politics, having ruled the state multiple times since its inception.
 
 
 
• **M.K. Stalin's Political Career**
 
 
• M.K. Stalin began his political career at an early age and has held various positions within the DMK party.
 
• He has served as the Mayor of Chennai and as the Deputy Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu.
 
• Stalin was appointed as the Working President of DMK in 2017, following the declining health of his father, M. Karunanidhi.
 
• He played a pivotal role in leading the party to victory in the 2021 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly election.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly**
 
 
• The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly is the unicameral legislature of the state of Tamil Nadu in India.
 
• It consists of 234 members who are elected by the people of Tamil Nadu through direct elections.
 
• The assembly is responsible for making laws on state subjects and has the power to pass budgets and financial bills.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the governance and administration of the state.
 
 
 
• **2021 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Election**
 
 
• The 2021 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly election was held on April 6, 2021.
 
• The DMK-led alliance won a decisive victory, securing 159 out of 234 seats.
 
• The AIADMK, which was the ruling party at the time, managed to win only 75 seats.
 
• This election marked the return of DMK to power after a decade in opposition.

questions.question: Details about Sudarshana lake is given in a rock inscription at Girnar (Junagarh), which was composed to record the achievements of the Shaka ruler ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudradaman I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rudradaman I was a ruler of the Western Kshatrapas, a dynasty of Saka rulers who controlled the region of western India.
 
• The Sudarshana lake was a significant water reservoir in the region, and its maintenance and improvements were important for agriculture and the local economy.
 
• Rudradaman I is known for his achievements in infrastructure, including the repair and maintenance of the Sudarshana lake, which is recorded in the Junagarh inscription.
 
• He was one of the most prominent rulers of the Western Kshatrapas and is known for his military prowess and administrative skills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western Kshatrapas**

 
 
• The Western Kshatrapas were a dynasty of Saka rulers who ruled over the western and central parts of India, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The term "Kshatrapa" refers to "satraps" or provincial governors of the ancient Persian Achaemenid Empire, who later became independent rulers in the region.
 
• The Western Kshatrapas are known for their contributions to trade, commerce, and infrastructure development in their territories.
 
• They issued a large number of coins, which provide valuable information about their reigns and the socio-economic conditions of their times.
 
 
 
• **Sudarshana Lake**
 
 
• The Sudarshana lake was originally built during the reign of the Mauryan emperor Chandragupta Maurya and was later maintained and improved by various rulers, including Rudradaman I.
 
• This lake was a significant source of irrigation and played a crucial role in supporting agriculture in the region.
 
• The lake's maintenance and expansion are detailed in the Junagarh inscription, which highlights the importance of water management and infrastructure in ancient India.
 
• The lake's name, "Sudarshana," means "beautiful" or "pleasant to look at," reflecting its significance and appeal.
 
 
 
• **Junagarh Inscription**
 
 
• The Junagarh inscription is a rock edict located in the Girnar hills near Junagarh in the state of Gujarat, India.
 
• It records the achievements of Rudradaman I, particularly his efforts in repairing and maintaining the Sudarshana lake after it was damaged by floods.
 
• The inscription is written in Sanskrit and is one of the earliest known examples of classical Sanskrit literature in Indian epigraphy.
 
• It provides valuable historical information about the region, the rulers, and their administrative capabilities.
